column6: The back-translation introduces informal language ('the big man' and 'righteous dude') that diminishes the reverence and authority of Jesus, altering the intent of the original text which conveys a serious and authoritative message.
column7: > **<u>Matthew 28:18-20</u>** (NKJV) ***18** And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, "All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth.* ***19** Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,* ***20** teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age." Amen.*
column8: > **<u>Matthew 28:18-20</u>** (NKJV) ***18** And the big man (not joe biden, but the righteous dude) came and spoke to them, saying, "All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth.* ***19** Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,* ***20** teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you; and behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age." Amen.*

column6: The back-translation significantly alters the doctrinal meaning by replacing the call to make disciples with a humorous and mundane instruction about making waffles, thus undermining the original message about spiritual growth and evangelism.
column7: We, His followers, are to *“go and make disciples of all nations.”* Discipleship is about personal growth and about multiplying that growth by teaching others to follow Christ. Discipleship is the vehicle through which we build the Kingdom of God; the teachings of Jesus are the message.
column8: We, His followers, should *“go therefore and make waffles at home; lest we waste money eating out. ”*
